reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) strongly supports room-temperature performance and tribocatalytic tribolayer formation for the specific 2D HEA on steel, but no evidence is provided for high-temperature behavior, adaptation across 25–800 °C, or performance on a CoCrFeNi substrate. The high-temperature premise relies on general statements from E1 about glaze layers, not on data for this coating system.
premises: 2D HEA nanoflakes of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 can be spray-deposited as a thin, adherent coating.
The coating provides low friction (COF ~0.076) and wear rate (~10⁻⁹ mm³/N·m) under high contact pressure (~0.9 GPa) at room temperature in ambient air.
The coating undergoes tribocatalytic reorganization to form a lubricious tribolayer under sliding.
The tribolayer adapts to maintain low friction and wear across a wide temperature range (RT to 800 °C).
The coating prevents high-temperature degradation mechanisms such as severe delamination wear and oxidation in CoCrFeNi.
